name: Sandwalking

sections.body: Sandwalking is the human answer to maker country. Instead of cancelling the worm system, it teaches the player that survival on Arrakis is earned through discipline and technique.
sections.title: Overview

sections.body: The skill gives Fremen starts a sense of lived adaptation. Colonists are not dropped onto Arrakis as blank survivors. They begin with cultural knowledge that changes how they move through danger.
sections.title: Skill

sections.body: The important design choice is what sandwalking does not solve. Machines still rumble, harvest still carries risk, and open sand remains hostile. That keeps the system from trivializing the desert.
sections.title: Limits

sections.body: The curve rewards progression in a way the player can feel on every crossing. Higher skill means fewer needless calls to the maker, which turns practice into security without making it magic.

summary: Sandwalking is the discipline that lets human life exist on Arrakis without pretending the desert has become safe. It reduces personal vibration, but never excuses carelessness.
